name: Information Commissioner's Office

summary.text: The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) is the UK's data protection regulator. From 2017 it ran an investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns, which covered Cambridge Analytica, SCL Elections, Facebook, Leave.EU, Eldon Insurance, AggregateIQ and others. It reported to Parliament on 6 November 2018, fined Facebook £500,000 (the maximum under the Data Protection Act 1998) on 25 October 2018, served an enforcement notice on SCL Elections in May 2018 that led to a prosecution and guilty plea in January 2019, fined Leave.EU and Eldon Insurance in February 2019, and closed the investigation with a letter from Commissioner Elizabeth Denham to the DCMS Committee dated 2 October 2020.

facts.claim: On 6 November 2018 the ICO published its report to Parliament, 'Investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns', summarising an investigation that covered online social media platforms, data brokers, analytics firms, academic institutions, political parties and campaign groups; its headline finding was that there were risks in how many political parties processed personal data.
facts.quote: The ICO's November 2018 report to Parliament, dated 6 November 2018, summarised its investigation into data analytics in political campaigns.

sources.title: Investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns: A report to Parliament
Blog: Information Commissioner's report brings the ICO's investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns up to date

facts.claim: The ICO issued a monetary penalty notice to Facebook on 25 October 2018 imposing a fine of £500,000, the maximum available under the Data Protection Act 1998, for lack of transparency and security issues relating to the harvesting of users' data.
facts.quote: The ICO issued a monetary penalty notice to Facebook, imposing a fine of £500,000 on 25 October 2018. The report says the fine was the maximum monetary penalty available under the previous data protection law, for lack of transparency and security issues relating to the harvesting of data.

sources.title: Investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns: A report to Parliament

facts.claim: In May 2018 the ICO served an enforcement notice on SCL Elections over a subject access request made by Professor David Carroll, a US citizen; the company did not comply by the 3 June 2018 deadline and the ICO brought criminal proceedings against it.
facts.quote: It was served on SCL Elections in May 2018 over a subject access request from Professor David Carroll. The company did not comply with the terms of the notice by the 3 June 2018 deadline. The ICO then pursued criminal proceedings against the company as the corporate entity responsible.

sources.title: Investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns: A report to Parliament

facts.claim: In January 2019 SCL Elections pleaded guilty to an offence under the Data Protection Act 1998 for failing to respond to the ICO's enforcement notice and was ordered to pay a £15,000 fine, £6,000 in costs and a £170 victim surcharge; Commissioner Elizabeth Denham said the case showed there are consequences for ignoring the law.
facts.quote: SCL Elections pleaded guilty to an offence under the Data Protection Act 1998 for failing to respond to an ICO enforcement notice issued in May 2018. It was ordered to pay a £15,000 fine to the ICO, £6,000 in costs and a victim surcharge of £170.

sources.title: The ICO 1-0 Cambridge Analytica
SCL Elections fined by ICO

facts.claim: In February 2019 the ICO fined Leave.EU a total of £60,000 and Eldon Insurance £60,000 under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003: £15,000 against Leave.EU for using Eldon customers' details to send almost 300,000 political marketing messages, and £45,000 against Leave.EU and £60,000 against Eldon for two direct-marketing campaigns that sent over one million emails to Leave.EU subscribers without sufficient consent.
facts.quote: Leave.EU used Eldon Insurance customers' details unlawfully to send almost 300,000 political marketing messages. Leave.EU has been fined 15,000 pounds for this breach. The campaigns involved the sending of over 1 million emails to Leave.EU subscribers without sufficient consent. Leave.EU has been fined 45,000 pounds and Eldon Insurance has been fined 60,000 pounds for the breach.

sources.title: ICO fines Leave.EU and Eldon Insurance for sending emails without consent
UK ICO fines and audits Leave.EU and Eldon Insurance

facts.claim: The ICO's 2018 report concluded there was no evidence of a working relationship between Cambridge Analytica and Leave.EU proceeding beyond an initial phase, while noting that both sides acknowledged an early exploration of working together and that allegations had been made about paid work on UKIP membership data in 2015.
facts.quote: The ICO concluded there was no evidence of a working relationship between CA and Leave.EU proceeding beyond this initial phase. Both sides had acknowledged an early exploration of working together

sources.title: Investigation into the use of data analytics in political campaigns: A report to Parliament

facts.claim: In her closing letter to the DCMS Committee chair Julian Knight MP dated 2 October 2020, Commissioner Elizabeth Denham wrote that analysis of material from Cambridge Analytica's servers did not produce additional evidence of Russian involvement, that SCL/CA were not part of the UK referendum campaign beyond initial enquiries about UKIP data, and that the methods SCL used were in the main well-recognised processes using commonly available technology.
facts.quote: Her letter states that the analysis of material on the Cambridge Analytica servers did not produce any additional evidence of Russian involvement. ... Denham told the committee that the methods SCL were using were, in the main, well recognised processes using commonly available technology.

sources.title: Letter from the Information Commissioner to Julian Knight MP, Chair of the DCMS Committee
Cambridge Analytica 'not involved' in EU referendum, finds ICO

facts.claim: The 2020 closing letter also states that Cambridge Analytica appeared to have done a limited amount of work for Leave.EU involving analysis of UKIP membership data rather than data obtained from Facebook or GSR, and that the Commissioner identified no significant breaches meeting the threshold for formal regulatory action.
facts.quote: Cambridge Analytica did appear to do a limited amount of work for Leave.EU but this involved the analysis of UKIP membership data rather than data obtained from Facebook or GSR.

openQuestions: The ICO's own press release on the January 2019 SCL Elections guilty plea and the court venue were not located; the fine breakdown (£15,000 plus £6,000 costs and £170 surcharge) is from legal and trade-press accounts, while the ICO's 2020 letter gives the figure as £18,000.
The Facebook monetary penalty notice itself (25 October 2018) should be cited directly; it is described here via the November 2018 report to Parliament.
The brief lists this entity as 'information-commissioners-office'; the repository's slug function produces 'information-commissioner-s-office' from the seed name, which is the id used here.
